name: long_press_reset
summary: Hold a button for seconds to reset an RP2350 into its USB bootloader: an RC timer, a Schmitt buffer, and two N-FETs on BOOTSEL and RUN
note: From simple_earring rev 2 (vendored with the bolt earring: boards/bolt-earring/vendor/simple_earring/scripts/circuit.py, whose comments give the reasons and the corner simulations behind each value), where it replaced the BOOTSEL key. IN is high while the button is held (power_latch's PRESSED). R_TMR charges C_TMR (tau 6.8 s nominal; simple_earring's corners give 2-11 s) and D_DIS empties it the moment IN falls, so holds do not add up. U1, two Schmitt inverters, turns BOOT_TMR into one clean rising edge on LONG. LONG drives Q_BOOT, which pulls BOOTSEL low (through the MCU's own 1 kohm to QSPI_SS) for as long as the button is held; C_KICK and R_KICK differentiate LONG's edge into a ~10 ms pulse on Q_RUN's gate, which pulls RUN low. The chip resets and its boot ROM finds QSPI_SS strapped low. On a battery board whose MCU holds the power latch, the reset also drops the hold, so the board turns off on release: a hardware force-off. Everything runs from VDD, so the block draws nothing with the board off. R_TMR is large so U1's input leakage stays small next to the charge current; IN's source must hold IN low against it (power_latch's R_SENSE).

D_DIS.note: 1 cathode on IN, 2 anode on BOOT_TMR

C_TMR.note: The timer's capacitor; X5R, so its value moves with temperature and bias

U1.note: 1A pin 1, 1Y pin 6, 2A pin 3, 2Y pin 4, VCC 5, GND 2

Q_BOOT.note: Pulls BOOTSEL low while LONG is high

Q_RUN.note: Pulls RUN low for the pulse

IN.note: High while the button is held

BOOTSEL.note: Open drain: to the RP2350's BOOTSEL resistor, the far end from QSPI_SS

RUN.note: Open drain: to the RP2350's RUN, which needs its pull-up

citations.figure: SOD-323 outline with a band at one end, and the diode symbol; no pin numbers.
citations.note: D_DIS's cathode is the band end. KiCad's D_SOD-323 puts the cathode on pad 1, and Diode:1N4148WS (like Device:D) has K 1, A 2.
Reverse current max: D_DIS is reverse-biased while IN is high and the timer charges, and leaks two orders of magnitude less than R_TMR's ~3 uA charge current.

citations.note: Table 3, the same for every package (the GW is SOT363, TSSOP6). KiCad's 74LVC2G14 symbol uses the same numbers.
BOOT_TMR's seconds-long RC ramp is a legal input.

VT+ (positive-going threshold) at VCC 3.0 V, min / typ / max at -40 to +85 °C, then min / max at -40 to +125 °C. The table has no 3.3 V row: at 4.5 V VT+ is 1.90 / 2.47 / 3.10 V, so at 3.3 V it lies between the two rows.

citations.note: Typ and max, -40 to +85 °C: the leakage R_TMR's charge current must dwarf, and which IN's source must hold BOOT_TMR low against through R_TMR.
Q_BOOT and Q_RUN. Table-2; KiCad's BSS138 symbol (Q_NMOS_GSD) is G 1, S 2, D 3 as well.

citations.quote: Gate Threshold Voltage VGS(TH) VGS=VDS, ID=250uA 0.8 1.0 1.5 V
citations.note: Q_RUN's gate pulse ends when RUN_KICK decays through this threshold: C_KICK x R_KICK is 10 ms, and from a 3.3 V edge the pulse lasts RC x ln(3.3 V / VGS(th)), about 8-14 ms over 0.8-1.5 V.
